claims.claim: In Pompeii, a victim found wearing a gold bracelet, beside a small child, was long described as a mother.
claims.source_checked: Pilli et al. 2024, Current Biology 34(22), doi:10.1016/j.cub.2024.10.007; full text read via Firecrawl research index (pmid:39515325), sections 'House of the Golden Bracelet' and 'Combined genetic and osteological findings...'
claims.note: Paper: 1974 find, 'two adults (Individuals 50 and 52) and a young child (Individual 51), apparently standing on Individual 52's hip. Individual 52 was traditionally interpreted as a woman and mother, due to the association with the child, and an intricate golden bracelet ... worn on one arm'. 'Beside' is softer than 'standing on the hip' but not contradicted; 'small child' fits a 5-6-year-old; 'long described' fits 'traditionally interpreted' since 1974 and spread 'through museal exhibitions and educational and publicity materials'. House is in Regio VI, Pompeii. The publisher page (doi.org) timed out through Firecrawl; the indexed full text was read instead.

claims.claim: A4: what the hook leaves with a viewer who swipes at second two (and at the end of the first sentence)
claims.source_checked: Same as claim 1; no alignment file exists yet for this VO (no src/generated/pompeii-casts.alignment.json), so timing is estimated
claims.note: At ~2.5-3 words/s the viewer has heard about 'In Pompeii, a victim found wearing a gold...' by 2 s: no claim yet. The whole first sentence is true as stated: it asserts only that the victim was described as a mother, not that the victim was one, and 'long described as' signals a reading, not a fact. Re-check with word timings once the VO is recorded.

claims.claim: Ancient DNA says it was a man, with no sign he was related to the child.
claims.source_checked: Pilli et al. 2024 (pmid:39515325), 'House of the Golden Bracelet' results, Table 1, Discussion
claims.note: 'All individuals were sexed as genetically male, including the presumed female adult (Individual 52)'; nuclear sexing succeeded for 52 (Table 1: genetic sex M, 364,533 SNPs). 52 was a 'younger middle-aged adult', so 'a man' fits. 'both the mitochondrial DNA and whole genome data found no evidence of biological relatedness, at least up to the third degree, between any of the individuals'; Discussion: 'are in fact not genetically related'. 'No sign' = 'no evidence' and does not exceed the paper.

claims.claim: Two victims found in an embrace were imagined as sisters, or a mother and daughter.
claims.source_checked: Pilli et al. 2024 (pmid:39515325), 'House of the Cryptoporticus'
claims.note: The paper says the two (Individuals 21 and 22, excavated 1914) 'were found close to each other in what was interpreted as an embrace'. The embrace is itself one of the interpretations under test, and the script's next lines say restorers may have reworked poses; stating 'found in an embrace' as fact breaks A3/A5 (record vs story). Change to e.g. 'Two victims found close together, read as an embrace, were imagined as sisters, or a mother and daughter.' The hypotheses part is accurate ('two sisters, mother and daughter, or lovers'); dropping 'lovers' is acceptable because line 5 claims only that one was male, not that every reading was refuted, but the SOURCES block should keep saying so.

claims.claim: One of them was genetically male.
claims.source_checked: Pilli et al. 2024 (pmid:39515325), 'House of the Cryptoporticus', Table 1
claims.note: 'The nuclear genetic analysis was successful only for Individual 22 and revealed he was male, excluding the possibility that the pair of victims were sisters or mother and daughter.' Table 1: cast 22, House of the Cryptoporticus, genetic sex M. 'One of them' correctly avoids implying Individual 21 was sexed.

claims.claim: The casts were made from 1863 on, by pouring plaster into the hollows the bodies left in the ash.
claims.source_checked: Pilli et al. 2024 (pmid:39515325), STAR Methods 'Plaster casts' and Introduction
claims.note: Methods: 'In 1863 Fiorelli set up a method to realize plaster casts on some of the victims of the eruption, pouring liquid chalk into the voids left by the bodies in the hardened ash'. Introduction: 'pouring liquid plaster into the voids left by decay of the victims' soft tissue'; 104 casts made with Fiorelli's method. The two casts in the script come from 1914 and 1974 finds, consistent with 'from 1863 on'.

claims.claim: Over the years, restorers reworked some of them, possibly to tell those very stories.
claims.source_checked: Pilli et al. 2024 (pmid:39515325), Introduction and final Discussion paragraph
claims.note: First half is supported: 'The casts had been considerably manipulated and likely creatively restored in the past'; 'restorers who chose to enhance or alter some features of the bodies' shapes'. Second half overstates: the paper says only 'it is possible that the exploitation of the casts as vehicles for storytelling led to the manipulation of their poses and relative positioning by restorers' - storytelling in general. It does not say the Golden Bracelet or Cryptoporticus casts were altered, nor that restorers acted to tell the mother or sisters stories. 'Those very stories' ties the speculation to these two narratives. Change to e.g. 'Over the years, restorers reworked some of them, possibly to make them tell a story.' (keeps the paper's 'possible', drops the specific link).

claims.claim: The DNA does not tell us who these people were. It tells us the old stories were guesses.
claims.source_checked: Pilli et al. 2024 (pmid:39515325), Introduction (study aims) and final Discussion paragraph
claims.note: Aims: to test 'interpretations suggested in the absence of genetic data about the identity of the victims and their relations to each other, based on the shape and position of the bodies'. Discussion: 'this study illustrates how unreliable narratives based on limited evidence can be' and warns against 'establishing new narratives that might also misrepresent these people's lived experiences'. 'Guesses' is a fair paraphrase of interpretations made without that evidence, and understates rather than overstates (the paper says the kinship narrative was falsified). 'The old stories' reads, in context, as the two just told, both of which the DNA contradicted; it should not be broadened to all cast interpretations (e.g. Individual 25's male sex was confirmed).
